english_classification.chapter_title: Concerning Wisdom; it is far superior when on the Tongue than in the Heart of the Person.
english_classification.chapter_note: This chapter contains no discernible cosmological-correspondential substrate. Teaching purity is 0.000 — the pipeline detected zero substrate vocabulary across all 17 paragraphs. The chapter is a self-contained Manichaean pedagogical dialogue using two natural SIMILES (child birth, fire in wood) to illustrate why wisdom is superior when proclaimed vs. hidden in the heart. Critically, the teaching uses simile ('like') rather than correspondential identity ('is'), distinguishing it from the substrate voice which directly identifies (e.g. 'The King of Wind IS eagle-face'). Both sides of every mapping remain in the natural/human domain (womb→open air, hidden fire→revealed fire) applied to epistemology (hidden wisdom→proclaimed wisdom) — no cosmic domains are mapped. The sole cosmic concept ('the Mind'/Nous in ¶16) is used illustratively, not systematically. The two-cycle dialogue structure (question→analogical answer→second question→extended analogies) appears to be an original Manichaean composition rather than a compilation wrapping pre-existing cosmic teaching.
